label: PF Backlog 603
title: EDP-22: Benchmarks/SLOs + EXPLAIN(ANALYZE,BUFFERS) tuning + observability + quotas + graceful degradation (DB/object/cache/queue)

decisions.note: HIL approved a third independent design review to verify fixes for the 15 Gate 1.5 findings.
HIL approved EDP-22 Gate 1 after design review and implementation evidence.

brief.problem: No repeatable performance baselines, SLOs, or degradation strategy exist across DB/object/cache/queue.
brief.what_adds: Benchmark harness, EXPLAIN-based tuning, observability, quotas, and graceful degradation switches.
brief.why: Enterprise scale claims need evidence and operational guardrails.
brief.who_feels: Operators, SREs, and customers hitting slow paths.

objective: Establish performance benchmarks/SLOs, EXPLAIN(ANALYZE,BUFFERS)-based tuning, observability, quotas, and graceful degradation for DB, object store, cache, and queue.
acceptance_criteria: Benchmark suite produces repeatable results for each store with recorded baselines
EXPLAIN(ANALYZE,BUFFERS) capture tooling available and sampling-only in prod
Quota enforcement and degradation switches demonstrated per store
out_of_scope: Data-model changes of the stores themselves
approach: Define workload scenarios, capture EXPLAIN baselines, wire metrics, add quota checks and store-specific degradation switches.

prior_decisions: EDP-06 baseline harness landed with a Sink seam reserved for EDP-22.
EDP-19/20/21 stores and EDP-18 migration framework are complete.
assumptions: SLO numbers are set from measured local baselines first.
divergences: EDP-22 does not add replicas or partitioning; it produces the evidence those decisions require.
open_questions: Which deployment-specific SLO targets should override conservative defaults?

impact_review.claim: API CHECK: no new public API; benchmark CLI and ops tooling only.
AC CHECK: four acceptance criteria mapped to four slices.
LANGUAGE CHECK: shipped performance tooling in Go; EXPLAIN helper in Python tooling.
SLO CHECK: bounded metric labels per store/scenario; no tenant labels.
DEGRADATION CHECK: switches must fail closed and be observable.

verification: benchmark CLI produces baseline JSON and Prometheus text
risks: SLO thresholds can be aspirational without measured baselines.
EXPLAIN ANALYZE must be sampling-only in production.
Degradation switches can mask failures if not bounded and alerted.
Benchmark scenarios must remain deterministic and tenant-safe.
rollback: Benchmarks and metrics are additive; degradation switches default off and can be disabled per store.
evidence: Candidate analyzers show existing analysis patterns

analysis.implementation_strategy: Build a perf/observability capability: benchmark harness reusing core/code_analyzer.py and core/product_analyzer.py patterns, EXPLAIN(ANALYZE,BUFFERS) capture tooling, metric emission on DB/object/cache/queue, quota enforcement hooks, and degradation switches on each store.
dependency_findings: BLOCKS nothing; later items benefit from SLOs
conflict_findings: Touches read/write paths of every store — sequence strictly after EDP-19..21 land
Concurrent edit risk with BI-PF-1315 reconciliation probes
duplication_findings: core/code_analyzer.py/product_analyzer.py are analyzers, not perf harnesses — only reuse metric/format patterns
BI-PF-1312 audit metrics may overlap — reuse rather than re-instrument
analysis.rationale: Cross-cutting performance capability that must follow all store work; classified as new capability since no existing benchmarking component fits.
assumptions: Stores expose queryable interfaces after EDP-19..21
Metrics pipeline (Prometheus/OTel) exists or is in scope-lite
risks: No baseline metrics exist — SLO targets may be aspirational
EXPLAIN overhead must be sampling-only in prod
evidence: Candidate analyzers show existing analysis patterns
missing_info: Target SLO numbers and acceptable latency budgets
Existing metrics/observability stack to plug into

context_review.reason: Approach is clear but depends on upstream EDP-19..21 stores landing first.

api_impact.reason: Internal benchmark CLI, SLO rules, and ops tooling; no product API surface.

tier_reasons: cross-cutting DB/object/cache/queue performance, SLO, quota, and degradation surface
language_rule: Go for shipped benchmark/SLO code; Python only for repo ops tooling.

requirements: Benchmark suite produces repeatable results for each store with recorded baselines
EXPLAIN(ANALYZE,BUFFERS) capture tooling available and sampling-only in prod
Quota enforcement and degradation switches demonstrated per store
scope: Slice 1: benchmark CLI + repeatability protocol + versioned baseline artifact schema.
Slice 2: EXPLAIN(ANALYZE,BUFFERS) capture with read-only role, allowlist, timeout, rollback, redaction, retention, audit, rate/load caps.
Slice 3: per-store metrics + quota enforcement + bounded degradation with persistent expiry.
Slice 4: generate SLO rules/dashboard from measured baselines and validate with promtool/Grafana schema checks.
non_goals: No read replicas, partitioning, or region cells (EDP-24).
No production EXPLAIN sampling without an explicit switch.
invariants: Benchmark labels never include tenant IDs; run timestamp is an unlabeled gauge, not a label.
Benchmarks use PF_BENCH_DSN with pf_readonly (NOSUPERUSER/NOBYPASSRLS), synthetic t-bench tenant, and deterministic cleanup.
Missing DSN fails closed unless --allow-skip records BENCH_STORE_SKIPPED as non-success.
EXPLAIN runs are read-only, allowlisted, timed out, rolled back, redacted, audited, retained, and capped by both probability and per-minute/concurrency budgets.
Degradation requires owner, reason, expires_at, max_duration<=15m; expiry is reloaded and enforced; renewals are alerted and bounded.
SLO rules/dashboard are generated only after measured baselines; config references baseline IDs and validation checks drift.

api: No new public API; internal benchmark CLI only.
db: Uses existing stores; EXPLAIN ANALYZE only on sampled queries.

security: Bench/EXPLAIN DSN must be a read-only role (pf_readonly) with no superuser/bypassrls.
Benchmark labels exclude tenant IDs, DSNs, and secrets.
EXPLAIN uses static allowlisted SQL with no bound tenant parameters; output is redacted and access-controlled.
Degradation/config changes are operator-only; no public API.
Explain runs are recorded in an audit log with actor, statement label, sample decision, and artifact path; artifacts are access-controlled and retained per config.
EXPLAIN artifacts are written to access-controlled retention paths with owner/expiry metadata.
observability: Benchmark metrics: edp_bench_p50_ms/p95/p99/errors by bounded group/scenario; last run is edp_bench_last_run_unixtime (no labels).
Store metrics: edp_store_requests_total, errors, latency histogram, degraded gauge by bounded store label.
SLO rules and dashboard are generated from config/edp-slo.json and validated for drift/schema.
performance: Benchmarks declare warmup, iteration count, concurrency, deterministic seed, outlier policy, and host class.
EXPLAIN has sample probability <=0.05 plus max_per_minute and max_concurrent load-shed caps.
rollout: Benchmark scheduling and EXPLAIN sampling default off.
Enable per environment with operator-owned config and runbooks.
rollback: Disable sampling/scheduling and remove rules/dashboard; no schema change.
decisions: Use measured local baselines before tightening SLO thresholds.
guardrails: Instrument existing adapters; no new store.
learnings: EDP-06 deferred the Sink intentionally; EDP-22 supplies it.
open_questions: Deployment-specific SLO overrides are allowed only after a measured baseline and must reference the baseline ID.
Prometheus/Grafana intervals are deployment-owned; generation validates both.

coverage.adapter: bench CLI + baseline JSON + Prometheus sink
coverage.contract: six groups emit versioned baseline JSON and bounded p50/p95/p99 metrics; missing DSN fails unless explicit skip
allowlisted read-only capture, statement_timeout, rollback, production sample<=0.05, rate cap, redaction

coverage.adapter: Prometheus rules + Grafana dashboard + store metrics
coverage.contract: alerts/dashboard cover DB/object/cache/queue with freshness, latency, errors, degradation, quota; assets validate offline
per-store switch requires owner/reason/expiry, max 900s, expires fail closed, metrics/alert state
call_sites: store adapter -> degrade.Check -> fixed degraded error + observe metrics

proof_plan.red_evidence: Baseline CLI/SLO sink absent; EXPLAIN guard absent; degradation policy absent.
proof_plan.green_evidence: Benchmark CLI/SLO, EXPLAIN guard, store metrics, and degradation tests pass with measured baselines.

runtime_contract.trigger: scheduled operator benchmark or sampled EXPLAIN request
runtime_contract.adapter: edpsvc bench + Prometheus/Grafana + psycopg EXPLAIN tool
runtime_contract.contract: bounded, versioned baselines and sampled plans; no tenant labels
runtime_contract.failure_behavior: fail closed on regression/unsampled prod; fixed degradation errors
runtime_contract.observable_result: operators see latency/error/freshness/degradation alerts per store

api_contract: See EDP-22 design: no new schema; bounded labels; sampling-only EXPLAIN; degradation fail-closed.
audit: Benchmark runs, sampling decisions, redaction, and degradation start/expiry are logged/auditable.
backup_restore: No data-model change; benchmark and EXPLAIN artifacts follow existing backup/retention.
compatibility: New internal CLI/config; no public API change.
concurrency_idempotency: Baseline compare is deterministic for a fixed seed; EXPLAIN is read-only.
data_model: No DB schema change. Baseline artifacts: engineering/benchmarks/BI-PF-1314/<store>/<env>/<git-sha>.json with version, seed, warmup, ops, concurrency, host, duration, variance.
deployment_rollout: Benchmark scheduling/EXPLAIN sampling default off; enable with config + runbook.
Degradation is operator-owned, persistent, and auto-expires; SLO generation runs after baseline capture.
ownership: edpsvc owns bench/SLO/degrade; ops owns sample execution and dashboards.
performance_capacity: Measured baselines define thresholds; explicit ops/concurrency; bounded sampling.
prerequisites: EDP-06 Sink seam; EDP-19/20/21 stores; EDP-18 migration tooling.
quotas: Per-store quota denied/allowed counters; degradation is bounded and expires automatically.
rls_tenant: Bench/EXPLAIN DSNs use read-only non-bypass roles; no tenant parameters in EXPLAIN; labels contain no tenant IDs.
rollback_recovery: Disable benchmarks/sampling; remove rules/dashboard; degradation auto-expires.
security_model: Read-only least-privilege DB roles; redacted plans; operator-only controls.

BLOCKER: AC-3 is not designed: open question on whether object/cache/queue expose counters means per-store SLO dashboards/alerts cannot be shown to exist; no adapter instrumentation files are in scope.
AC-4 is not designed: quota enforcement and per-store degradation switches reference `go/edpsvc/internal/limits` but no affected file, config schema, or test defines quotas/switch behavior per store.
DB access for benchmark and EXPLAIN capture has no least-privilege/read-only role or RLS enforcement; “tenant-safe” invariant lacks a boundary control and risks admin/RLS-bypass DSNs.
MAJOR: AC-1 lacks baseline artifact definition: no storage location, versioning, environment fingerprint, variance tolerance, or retention for recorded baselines, so repeatability is not verifiable.
AC-1 failure case “missing DSN -> skipped scenarios” can produce a green run without per-store coverage; it should fail closed or record explicit skipped-store evidence.
AC-2 prod enforcement is underspecified: no environment detection and no hard production cap preventing `sample_rate=1.0`; sampling-only policy can be bypassed by config.
AC-2 `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` executes statements; no read-only transaction, statement allowlist, statement timeout, or rollback guard is defined.
AC-2 redaction of parameters/tenant data is declared but has no mechanism or test evidence; captured plans can leak literals/tenant data.
AC-3 validation is weak: Python config tests do not prove Prometheus rule semantics, alert lead time, or Grafana dashboard/schema validity; scrape/eval intervals remain open.
AC-4 “bounded” degradation is not quantified: no max duration, auto-expiry, quota-denied metric, or alert-routing handoff is defined.
SLO thresholds are not tied to measured baselines; open deployment overrides and aspirational values risk alert noise or missed regressions.
MINOR: Benchmark reconstruction metadata is incomplete: concurrency, dataset seed/size, host class, and run duration should be recorded with baselines.
Mixing SLO policy and runtime quota/degradation policy in `config/edp-slo.json` blurs ownership and rollback boundaries.
Captured EXPLAIN artifacts need explicit retention and access-control policy beyond “redacted”.
Quota enforcement observability lacks clear denied/allowed counters and bounded store labels.
NIT: `scripts/dev/db_explain_capture.py` is acceptable as tooling, but its prod guardrails should be documented alongside ops runbooks.
Single evidence doc `docs/EDP-22-BENCHMARKS-SLOS.md` should index baseline artifacts, rule files, dashboards, and per-store proof.
SUMMARY: Design is directionally sound on bounded labels, fail-closed regression, and default-off rollout, but AC-3 and AC-4 are not yet demonstrable.
Top risks: missing per-store SLO/counter coverage, undefined quota/degradation implementation evidence, and insufficient DB privilege/RLS and EXPLAIN redaction controls.
AC-1/AC-2 need stronger repeatability, environment, sampling, and read-only execution contracts before Gate 1.5.

BLOCKER: AC-4 quota enforcement is not designed: no quota hook in `affected_files`, `call_sites`, or test matrix; `limits/quota.go` is only cited as evidence and remains out of scope, so “quota enforcement … demonstrated per store” cannot pass.

AC-1 can pass without per-store baselines: `--allow-skip` records skipped evidence but no gate/test rejects it, and the test matrix is only `go test ./...` with no repeat-run/variance or baseline-artifact validation.
MAJOR: AC-3/AC-4 review scope omits `go/edpsvc/internal/observe/metrics.go` and `go/edpsvc/internal/degrade/policy.go`, the declared entrypoints for store metrics and degradation; the binding review cannot verify those ACs.
AC-3 test matrix covers only `test_edp_slo_config.py`; `metrics_test.go` exists but store metric emission from `observe/metrics.go` is not part of AC-3 evidence.

AC-2 production EXPLAIN sampling relies on operator-run `scripts/dev/db_explain_capture.py`; no deployment path, persistent sampling switch, audit sink, access-control enforcement, or retention control is designed beyond assertions.

Benchmark tenant safety is underspecified: no synthetic tenant/fixture or RLS session context is defined, so a NOSUPERUSER/NOBYPASSRLS role with no tenant parameters may produce empty/error benchmarks or rely on unforced RLS.
SLO thresholds exist in both `config/edp-slo.json` and `ops/prometheus/edp-slo.rules.yml`; no single-source generation/contract is stated, so config/rule drift is likely.
MINOR: `edp_quota_denials_total{scope,store}` leaves `scope` undefined; if not allowlisted it is a high-cardinality label risk.
Failure matrix `BENCH_DSN_MISSING` wording/exit semantics are contradictory for `--allow-skip`; define whether skipped evidence is non-success.
Baseline and EXPLAIN artifact retention/access control are asserted but not specified in scoped files.
“Six store groups” vs DB/object/cache/queue mapping is unspecified; baseline artifact naming is not tied to a declared store enum.
No on-startup validation/compatibility check for `config/edp-slo.json` and `config/edp-degradation.json`; invalid config fails at runtime.
NIT: Metric naming mixes `edp_store_latency_ms_bucket` with `edp_bench_p95_ms`; ensure histogram/summary conventions are consistent.
`run_timestamp` in benchmark metrics may undermine baseline equality unless excluded from comparisons.
Docs are the only evidence for multiple ACs; add machine-checkable evidence references.
SUMMARY: Design is directionally sound: additive, read-only, bounded degradation, and no public API.
Gate-1 cannot approve AC-1/AC-4 as written; quota enforcement and repeatability/baseline evidence are materially missing.
Top risks: prod EXPLAIN sampling controls, metrics/degradation outside verifiable scope, and config/rule drift.

BLOCKER: AC-4 quota enforcement is not designed: `go/edpsvc/internal/limits/quota.go` is cited as evidence/control target but is absent from affected_files/review_scope, with no quota config, enforcement point, persistence/consistency model, or per-store behavioral test.

AC-2 control mapping is wrong: runtime entrypoint is Go `cmd/explain`/`explain.Capture`, but CTL-EXPLAIN-SAMPLING and AC-2 evidence/check target `scripts/dev/db_explain_capture.py`; sampling cap, allowlist, rollback, and redaction are not tied to the actual runtime path.
MAJOR: SLO rules/dashboard are delivered in Slice 1 while measured baselines arrive in Slice 4, contradicting the invariant that thresholds come from measured baselines; no baseline-to-config linkage or validation prevents aspirational SLOs.
Generated Prometheus rules and Grafana dashboard lack `promtool`/Grafana schema validation and drift checks in the test matrix, so the single-source config invariant is not enforced.
Degradation auto-expiry persistence and renewal limits are undefined; file-based config may not expire without reload, and repeated renewals can mask failures despite `max_duration<=15m`.
EXPLAIN sampling is probability-capped only; no global/per-query rate limit or load-shed budget means 0.05 sampling can still overload production at high QPS.

Benchmark repeatability protocol is underspecified: no warmup, iteration count, outlier policy, or deterministic dataset provisioning; “six store groups” is also not mapped to the AC’s DB/object/cache/queue stores.
AC-1 recorded baselines have no defined artifact schema/path per store; only `engineering/benchmarks/BI-PF-1314/README.md` is listed, so baseline evidence cannot be reviewed.
MINOR: `run_timestamp` is listed among benchmark metrics; if emitted as a label it violates the bounded-cardinality/no-high-cardinality-label invariant.
`failure_taxonomy` omits `BENCH_STORE_SKIPPED` and `CONFIG_INVALID`, which appear in the failure matrix.
Scope/component lists omit `go/edpsvc/internal/explain` and `cmd/explain` despite being declared files and AC-2 entrypoints.
EXPLAIN artifact retention, access-control, and redaction details are asserted but not concretely specified or tested.
Synthetic `t-bench` tenant provisioning/cleanup is not defined, so RLS-scoped non-empty-read assertions may be non-deterministic.
NIT: Only `docs/EDP-22-BENCHMARKS-SLOS.md` is listed as evidence; no operator runbook link for enabling sampling/degradation is declared.
`runtime_capability: false` on AC-2/AC-3/AC-4 coverage is unexplained and conflicts with “tooling available/demonstrated” acceptance language.
SUMMARY: Design direction is sound, but Gate-1 readiness is blocked by quota-enforcement and EXPLAIN control gaps.
Top risks: SLO thresholds not grounded in measured baselines, generated artifacts not validated, and degradation expiry/renewal semantics undefined.
Baseline artifact definition and per-store behavioral evidence need to be explicit before approval.

BLOCKER: AC-4 quota enforcement is entirely absent: no `internal/limits/quota.go`, no call sites, and nothing emits `edp_quota_allowed_total`/`edp_quota_denials_total` yet the alert `ProductForgeQuotaDenied` and dashboard panel 5 query them — AC-4 cannot be satisfied and the alert can never fire.

AC-1 baseline evidence declared in the contract (`engineering/benchmarks/BI-PF-1314/README.md`, `db/local/baseline.json`, `db/local/metrics.prom`) is not in the diff, and `config/edp-slo.json` contains thresholds with no baseline ID reference — violates the "SLO thresholds are set from measured baselines, not invented targets" invariant.

Store metrics and degradation are dead code: `observe.Recorder` and `degrade.Check` have no store-adapter call sites in the diff, so AC-3/AC-4 ("demonstrated per store") and the runtime contract `store adapter -> degrade.Check -> fixed degraded error + observe metrics` are unproven.
MAJOR: `bench.Compare` ignores `MaxError` when a result has an error (`if r.Err != "" { violation; continue }`), and `MaxError==0` is treated as "unset" in the group override — `max_errors` config is effectively dead.
`edp_store_latency_ms` is emitted as a last-value gauge via `Set`, not the histogram the observability contract requires; p95/p99 store SLOs are therefore impossible from this metric.
`edp_bench_errors_total` is written as 0/1 per run from a file sink — non-monotonic value under a `_total` counter name, so any `rate()`/`increase()` over it is wrong.
`observe.Recorder.Request` passes the caller-supplied `outcome` string straight into a label with no allowlist; only `store` is bounded, so cardinality/leak risk remains.
`ProductForgeBenchmarkLatencyRegression` hardcodes `> 500` while `config/edp-slo.json` sets db to 250 — rules are hand-written, not generated/validated for drift against config as Slice 4 requires.
`db_explain_capture.py` validates but never enforces `--per-minute` or any concurrency cap; the design invariant requires both probability and per-minute/concurrency budgets.

No audit record (actor, statement label, sample decision, artifact path) is produced for EXPLAIN runs, and `--out` writes to an arbitrary path with no retention/access-control enforcement — violates the audit/security contract.

Production cap is client-asserted: `--env` defaults to `PF_ENV`/`dev`, so a mis-set env allows `--sample-rate 0.1` against production; no separate explicit prod-enable switch as the non-goal requires.
`expires_at` renewal tracking/"renewals are alerted and bounded" is not implemented; `Config` is loaded once with no reload path, so operators cannot force-expire without a redeploy.

`config/edp-slo.schema.json` and `config/edp-degradation.schema.json` (contract + CTL-CONFIG-SCHEMA) are missing; `validate_edp_slo.py` only asserts alert names/panel presence, which is a tautological no-drift check.

`[OUT_OF_SCOPE]` `scripts/dev/review_ledger.py` now returns `[]` when no delta entries exist, silently disabling the `FULL_REVIEW_MISSING` gate for delta items (review-tooling behavior change, CL-002 territory).
MINOR: `config/edp-degradation.json` has `"stores": {}` — no per-store switch demonstrated and the test loop is vacuous.

Bench scenario semantics silently changed (`kind 'note'→'semantic'`, `acl_scope 'team'→'project'`) with no rationale; this alters what is measured and is close to the out-of-scope "data-model changes of the stores" line.
Freshness alert `time() - edp_bench_last_run_unixtime > 86400` never fires when the metric is absent; needs an `absent()` companion for a never-run suite.
`cmd/bench` default `-baseline config/edp-slo.json` is cwd-relative while the documented invocation runs from `go/edpsvc`; only the doc example's explicit path saves it.
No `Load` validation test for `expires_at` exceeding `max_duration_seconds` or for `max_errors` handling; `slo_test` only exercises `Compare` happy paths.
EXPLAIN redaction is regex-only (quoted literals, 4+ digit numbers); UUIDs/emails/timestamps outside quotes and `tenant_id` column values in plan output are not covered.
`max_errors` sentinel ambiguity and lack of `p50` budget in config mean partial budget semantics are undocumented.
NIT: `psycopg` is imported lazily with no pinned dependency/requirements entry for the tooling path.
`PrometheusSink` overwrites the sink file per run; there is no rotation or run-id comment header for traceability.
`validate_edp_slo.py` hardcodes `REQUIRED_GROUPS` including `artifact` while bench `scenarios()` groups are not cross-checked against config.
SUMMARY: Direction is right: bounded labels, fail-closed degradation errors, sampled EXPLAIN guard, and offline asset validation are solid foundations.

Not mergeable as-is: quota enforcement is missing entirely (AC-4), baseline evidence artifacts and baseline-ID linkage are absent (AC-1), and neither metrics nor degradation is wired into store adapters, so AC-3/AC-4 are only unit-tested, not demonstrated.

Observability contract mismatches (gauge latency, non-monotonic `_total`, hand-written rule thresholds) will let SLO drift go undetected; fix before the EDP-24 evidence gate relies on these baselines.

BLOCKER: `go/edpsvc/internal/observe/metrics.go`: after replacing `edp_store_latency_ms` with `ObserveHistogram`, the local `ms` and its negative clamp are left unused; Go rejects unused locals, so `go test ./...` cannot build.
`go/edpsvc/main.go` `cacheHandle`: `tenant` is required but never namespaces the key; `/admin/cache` GET/PUT/DELETE can read or overwrite another tenant’s cached bytes, bypassing tenant isolation.
MAJOR: `main.go`: any error from `degrade.NewPolicy` — including invalid `config/edp-degradation.json` — is swallowed and replaced by an empty policy instead of startup refusal, violating `CONFIG_INVALID` and fail-closed behavior.
`degrade/policy.go`: the new renewal counter is only returned by unused `RenewalCount`; no metric/alert/bound is emitted, so degradation can be renewed indefinitely without detection.
`cache/memory.go` + `main.go`: the store has no capacity/eviction bound and the handler always calls `Set` with `ttl=0`; the admin cache can grow without limit and never expires.
`bench/slo.go`: for `MaxError > 0`, any scenario with `Err != ""` is accepted, so a positive `max_errors` disables all error violations rather than bounding counts.

`scripts/dev/db_explain_capture.py`: `--state`/`--audit` are optional, the rate check is non-atomic, and there is no concurrency cap; the required per-minute/concurrency/audit guarantees remain bypassable.
`main.go` object store: quota is only reached via `/admin/object-store/conform` with `tenant=""`, so `Quota` is skipped for object store and real object operations remain unguarded.
MINOR: `db_explain_capture.py`: `rate_ok` consumes a slot even when sampling later skips the run, causing false `REFUSE` under normal sampled-out traffic.
`degrade/policy.go`: `Policy.Check` takes a global mutex and `os.Stat`s the config on every store operation, serializing hot-path calls and adding filesystem I/O.
`storeguard/guard.go`: `Do` checks only `g == nil`, not `g.Degrade`; a zero-value `Guard` panics instead of failing safe.
`validate_edp_slo.py`: sibling `import gen_edp_slo` inside `problems()` depends on `sys.path`; imported-module/pytest execution can fail with `ModuleNotFoundError`.
`validate_edp_slo.py`: alert presence is checked by substring, not exact rule/alert name, so a summary or comment can satisfy the check.
NIT: `db_explain_capture.py`: state/audit file opens are not context-managed; state writes are not atomic.
`audit` records are append-only with no rotation/fsync/retention enforcement in the tool.
`gen_edp_slo.py` hardcodes non-benchmark alerts while `validate_edp_slo.py` separately hardcodes required names; generation and validation can drift in the non-generated portion.
SUMMARY: The delta fixes several prior gaps (generated SLO rules, store guard wiring, histogram metrics, baseline references) but introduces a build blocker and a tenant-isolation bug in the new admin cache.
Remaining enterprise risks: silent degradation-config fallback, unbounded cache, incomplete `max_errors` semantics, and EXPLAIN controls that remain optional/non-atomic.
AC-4 per-store quota is not demonstrated for object store; the only object guard path skips quota with an empty tenant.
Blockers must be fixed before merge; majors should be fixed or explicitly accepted with runbook controls.
